text: Why did UTF-8 win over UTF-16 and UTF-32?
choices: It is the only encoding that covers all of Unicode
It uses less memory for every possible character
ASCII files are already valid UTF-8, each byte announces its role, and readers can resynchronize after damage
explanation: All three cover all of Unicode. UTF-8 is larger than UTF-16 for East Asian text, so it does not always win on size. What it has is compatibility — an ASCII file needs no conversion — plus self-synchronization and the guarantee that an ASCII byte never appears inside a multi-byte character, so byte-oriented software kept working.
